title: अष्टात्रिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Dhritarashtra is torn between shame and pride as Abhimanyu leads the Pandavas. Duhshasana, hearing Duryodhana's order, goes to face Abhimanyu, and the war drums sound.
summary.kn: ಅಭಿಮನ್ಯು ಪಾಂಡವರನ್ನು ಮುನ್ನಡೆಸುವಾಗ ಧೃತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರ ನಾಚಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಹೆಮ್ಮೆಯ ನಡುವೆ ಒದ್ದಾಡುತ್ತಾನೆ. ದುರ್ಯೋಧನನ ಆಜ್ಞೆ ಕೇಳಿ ದುಃಶಾಸನ ಅಭಿಮನ್ಯುವನ್ನು ಎದುರಿಸಲು ಹೋಗುತ್ತಾನೆ, ಯುದ್ಧವಾದ್ಯಗಳು ಮೊಳಗುತ್ತವೆ.
summary.hi: अभिमन्यु के पाण्डवों का नेतृत्व करते समय धृतराष्ट्र लज्जा और गर्व के बीच उलझते हैं। दुर्योधन का आदेश सुनकर दुःशासन अभिमन्यु का सामना करने जाता है और रणवाद्य बजते हैं।
summary.te: అభిమన్యుడు పాండవులను నడిపిస్తుండగా ధృతరాష్ట్రుడు సిగ్గు, గర్వం మధ్య కొట్టుమిట్టాడతాడు. దుర్యోధనుని ఆజ్ఞ విని దుశ్శాసనుడు అభిమన్యుని ఎదుర్కోవడానికి వెళతాడు, యుద్ధవాద్యాలు మోగుతాయి.
summary.ta: அபிமன்யு பாண்டவரை நடத்துகையில் த்ருதராஷ்டிரன் நாணத்துக்கும் பெருமைக்கும் இடையில் தவிக்கிறான். துரியோதனனின் ஆணை கேட்டுத் துச்சாசனன் அபிமன்யுவை எதிர்க்கச் செல்ல, போர்முரசுகள் முழங்குகின்றன.
summary.ml: അഭിമന്യു പാണ്ഡവരെ നയിക്കുമ്പോൾ ലജ്ജയും അഭിമാനവുമായി ധൃതരാഷ്ട്രർ പിടയുന്നു. ദുര്യോധനന്റെ കൽപ്പന കേട്ട് ദുശ്ശാസനൻ അഭിമന്യുവിനെ നേരിടാൻ ചെല്ലുന്നു; യുദ്ധഭേരികൾ മുഴങ്ങുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 7.38; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Tue Sep 22 2026

verses.text: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच

meaning.en: Dhritarashtra said:

verses.text:
द्वैधीभवति मे चित्तं ह्रिया तुष्ट्या च संजय ।
मम पुत्रस्य यत्सैन्यं सौभद्रः समवारयत् ॥

meaning.en: My mind is divided, Sanjaya, between shame and satisfaction, at how Subhadra's son held back my son's army.

verses.text:
विस्तरेणैव मे शंस सर्वं गावल्गणे पुनः ।
विक्रीडितं कुमारस्य स्कन्दस्येवासुरैः सह ॥

meaning.en: Tell me everything again, Sanjaya, in detail, the sport of that young man, like Skanda with the Asuras.

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
हन्त ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि विमर्दमतिदारुणम् ।
एकस्य च बहूनां च यथासीत्तुमुलो रणः ॥

meaning.en: Alas, I will tell you of that terrible crush, how the tumultuous battle between one and many went.

verses.text:
अभिमन्युः कृतोत्साहः कृतोत्साहानरिंदमान् ।
रथस्थो रथिनः सर्वांस्तावकानप्यहर्षयत् ॥

meaning.en: Abhimanyu in his chariot, with zeal, delighted even your chariot-warriors, though they were zealous enemy-tamers.

verses.text:
द्रोणं कर्णं कृपं शल्यं द्रौणिं भोजं बृहद्बलम् ।
दुर्योधनं सौमदत्तिं शकुनिं च महाबलम् ॥

meaning.en: Drona, Karna, Kripa, Shalya, Drona's son, Bhoja, Brihadbala, Duryodhana, Somadatta's son and mighty Shakuni,

verses.text:
नानानृपान्नृपसुतान्सैन्यानि विविधानि च ।
अलातचक्रवत्सर्वांश्चरन्बाणैः समभ्ययात् ॥

meaning.en: and many kings and princes and armies of every kind, he attacked, ranging with arrows like a whirling firebrand.

verses.text:
निघ्नन्नमित्रान्सौभद्रः परमास्त्रः प्रतापवान् ।
अदर्शयत तेजस्वी दिक्षु सर्वासु भारत ॥

meaning.en: Killing his enemies, mighty and splendid, Subhadra's son, master of the highest weapons, showed himself in all directions, O Bharata.

verses.text:
तद्दृष्ट्वा चरितं तस्य सौभद्रस्यामितौजसः ।
समकम्पन्त सैन्यानि त्वदीयानि पुनः पुनः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that conduct of the boundlessly powerful son of Subhadra, your armies trembled again and again.

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीन्महाप्राज्ञो भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान् ।
हर्षेणोत्फुल्लनयनः कृपमाभाष्य सत्वरम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the wise, mighty Bharadvaja's son, his eyes wide with delight, said quickly to Kripa,

verses.text:
घट्टयन्निव मर्माणि तव पुत्रस्य मारिष ।
अभिमन्युं रणे दृष्ट्वा तदा रणविशारदम् ॥

meaning.en: as if touching the vitals of your son, seeing Abhimanyu, skilled in war, in the battle:

verses.text:
एष गच्छति सौभद्रः पार्थानामग्रतो युवा ।
नन्दयन्सुहृदः सर्वान्राजानं च युधिष्ठिरम् ॥

meaning.en: "This young Subhadra's son goes at the head of the Parthas, delighting all his friends, King Yudhishthira,

verses.text:
नकुलं सहदेवं च भीमसेनं च पाण्डवम् ।
बन्धून्संबन्धिनश्चान्यान्मध्यस्थान्सुहृदस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: Nakula, Sahadeva, the Pandava Bhimasena, relatives, in-laws, neutrals and friends."

verses.text:
नास्य युद्धे समं मन्ये कंचिदन्यं धनुर्धरम् ।
इच्छन्हन्यादिमां सेनां किमर्थमपि नेच्छति ॥

meaning.en: "I think no other archer is equal to him in battle. If he wished, he could kill this army; why he does not wish it, I cannot say."

verses.text:
द्रोणस्य प्रीतिसंयुक्तं श्रुत्वा वाक्यं तवात्मजः ।
आर्जुनिं प्रति संक्रुद्धो द्रोणं दृष्ट्वा स्मयन्निव ॥

meaning.en: Hearing Drona's affectionate words, your son, angry at Arjuna's son, looked at Drona as if smiling,

verses.text:
अथ दुर्योधनः कर्णमब्रवीद्बाह्लिकं कृपम् ।
दुःसासनं मद्रराजं तांस्तांश्चान्यान्महारथान् ॥

meaning.en: and Duryodhana said to Karna, Bahlika, Kripa, Duhshasana, the Madra king and other great chariot-warriors:

verses.text:
सर्वमूर्धावसिक्तानामाचार्यो ब्रह्मवित्तमः ।
अर्जुनस्य सुतं मूढं नाभिहन्तुमिहेच्छति ॥

meaning.en: "The teacher, best of Brahmin knowers, does not wish to kill the foolish son of Arjuna, among all the kings anointed on their heads."

verses.text:
न ह्यस्य समरे मुच्येदन्तकोऽप्याततायिनः ।
किमङ्ग पुनरेवान्यो मर्त्यः सत्यं ब्रवीमि वः ॥

meaning.en: "For even Death would not escape him when he attacks in battle, let alone another mortal; I tell you the truth."

verses.text:
अर्जुनस्य सुतं त्वेष शिष्यत्वादभिरक्षति ।
पुत्राः शिष्याश्च दयितास्तदपत्यं च धर्मिणाम् ॥

meaning.en: "He protects Arjuna's son out of a teacher's love; sons and pupils are dear, and so are the children of righteous men."

verses.text:
संरक्ष्यमाणो द्रोणेन मन्यते वीर्यमात्मनः ।
आत्मसंभावितो मूढस्तं प्रमथ्नीत माचिरम् ॥

meaning.en: "Protected by Drona, that fool thinks highly of his own strength, conceited; crush him quickly."

verses.text:
एवमुक्तास्तु ते राज्ञा सात्वतीपुत्रमभ्ययुः ।
संरब्धास्तं जिघांसन्तो भारद्वाजस्य पश्यतः ॥

meaning.en: So told by the king, they went at the son of Satvati, in fury, wishing to kill him while Bharadvaja's son watched.

verses.text:
दुःशासनस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा दुर्योधनवचस्तदा ।
अब्रवीत्कुरुशार्दूलो दुर्योधनमिदं वचः ॥

meaning.en: Hearing Duryodhana's words, Duhshasana, tiger of the Kurus, said this to Duryodhana:

verses.text:
अहमेनं हनिष्यामि महाराज ब्रवीमि ते ।
मिषतां पाण्डुपुत्राणां पाञ्चालानां च पश्यताम् ।
ग्रसिष्याम्यद्य सौभद्रं यथा राहुर्दिवाकरम् ॥

meaning.en: "I will kill him, great king, I tell you. In the sight of the Pandavas and Panchalas, I will swallow Subhadra's son today as Rahu swallows the sun."

verses.text:
उत्क्रुश्य चाब्रवीद्वाक्यं कुरुराजमिदं पुनः ।
श्रुत्वा कृष्णौ मया ग्रस्तं सौभद्रमतिमानिनौ ।
गमिष्यतः प्रेतलोकं जीवलोकान्न संशयः ॥

meaning.en: Crying out, he spoke again to the Kuru king: "Hearing that Subhadra's son has been swallowed by me, the two proud Krishnas will go to the world of the dead, leaving the world of the living, without doubt."

verses.text:
तौ च श्रुत्वा मृतौ व्यक्तं पाण्डोः क्षेत्रोद्भवाः सुताः ।
एकाह्ना ससुहृद्वर्गाः क्लैब्याद्धास्यन्ति जीवितम् ॥

meaning.en: "And hearing of their death, the sons born on Pandu's field will, with their friends, give up their lives in a single day, from weakness."

verses.text:
तस्मादस्मिन्हते शत्रौ हताः सर्वेऽहितास्तव ।
शिवेन ध्याहि मा राजन्नेष हन्मि रिपुं तव ॥

meaning.en: "So when this enemy is killed, all your foes are killed. Be at ease, king; I will kill your enemy."

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा नदन्राजन्पुत्रो दुःशासनस्तव ।
सौभद्रमभ्ययात्क्रुद्धः शरवर्षैरवाकिरन् ॥

meaning.en: Having said this and roaring, your son Duhshasana, angry, went at Subhadra's son, covering him with showers of arrows.

verses.text:
तमभिक्रुद्धमायान्तं तव पुत्रमरिंदमः ।
अभिमन्युः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः षड्विंशत्या समर्पयत् ॥

meaning.en: The enemy-tamer Abhimanyu struck your angry son with twenty-six sharp arrows as he came on.

verses.text:
दुःशासनस्तु संक्रुद्धः प्रभिन्न इव कुञ्जरः ।
अयोधयत सौभद्रमभिमन्युश्च तं रणे ॥

meaning.en: Duhshasana, furious like a rutting elephant, fought Subhadra's son, and Abhimanyu fought him in the battle.

verses.text:
तौ मण्डलानि चित्राणि रथाभ्यां सव्यदक्षिणम् ।
चरमाणावयुध्येतां रथशिक्षाविशारदौ ॥

meaning.en: Those two, skilled in chariot-craft, moved their chariots in strange circles, to left and right, and fought.

verses.text:
अथ पणवमृदङ्गदुन्दुभीनां
कृकरमहानकभेरिझर्झराणाम् ।
निनदमतिभृशं नराः प्रचक्रु-
र्लवणजलोद्भवसिंहनादमिश्रम् ॥

meaning.en: Then men made a great noise of tabors, drums, kettledrums, krakacas, anakas, bheris and jharjharas, mixed with lion-roars, like the roar of the salt sea.
